summary: Merge sort over a singly linked list of string entries, storing the result head/tail back into a small result struct (this[0]=head, this[4]=tail, this[8]=head duplicate). Splits the list at its midpoint, recursively sorts each half via LinkedListMergeSort_4290, then merges the halves in ascending order using a byte-wise lexicographic comparison with a 2-byte stride (wide-character style); nodes whose string pointer is null fall back to byte_5EA438. Reconnects head and tail pointers after sorting. Used by DirectoryFileEnumerator during directory entry enumeration.

local_names.this: sort result struct holding head (this[0]), tail (this[4]) and head duplicate (this[8])
local_names.v3: current head pointer of the list being counted/sorted
local_names.v7: walk pointer advanced to the split midpoint node
local_names.v8: head of the right half captured at the midpoint split
local_names.v12: comparison string pointer from the right-half current node
local_names.v13: comparison string pointer from the left-half current node

operations.description: Proceeds only when the head pointer this[0] is non-null; otherwise skips counting and sorting.
Count list nodes by walking the next pointer at each node offset 4 until the null terminator.
Proceeds to split/sort only when the node count is at least 2; single-node lists need no sort.
Compute the split index as (node count / 2) minus 1.
Advance the walk pointer from the head by the split index to reach the midpoint node, following node offset 4.
Split the list: capture the right half head from the midpoint node's next pointer, then write 0 into that next pointer to null-terminate the left half.
Recursively sort the left half via LinkedListMergeSort_4290.
Recursively sort the right half via LinkedListMergeSort_4290.
Proceeds with the merge only when both sorted halves are non-null.
Resolve the comparison strings for the two head nodes, substituting the fallback &byte_5EA438 when a node's string pointer is null.
Byte-wise lexicographic comparison of the two strings in 2-byte steps, comparing low then high byte before advancing.
Derive the ordering sign from the comparison carry/equality flags to decide which node precedes.
Pick the head node of the merged output from either the left or the right half depending on the comparison sign.
Merge the remaining nodes of both halves, relinking node next pointers (offset 4) in ascending string order until one half is exhausted.
Write the sorted head into this[0].
Walk the merged list to its last node to recover the tail.
Write the recovered tail into this[4].
Write the sorted head again into this[8] as a duplicate head reference.
Return the trailing merge value (the remaining node reference or 0).
Invoked by DirectoryFileEnumerator to order directory entries.
